user.title: Connect to Emby
user.description:
Enter your Emby Server connection details.

You can find your **API Key** in your Emby Server Dashboard under **Advanced > API Keys**.

data_description.host: The IP address (e.g., 192.168.1.5) or hostname of your server.
data_description.api_key: A dedicated API key created in your Emby Dashboard.

clients.title: Choose Emby clients
clients.description: Pick the Emby apps and devices you want in Home Assistant. Emby often creates a new client for each browser, so you probably don't want them all.

data_description.clients: Each ticked client becomes a device in Home Assistant, even when it's offline. Clients you don't tick are ignored. You can change this later under the settings cog.

reconfigure.title: Update connection to {name}
reconfigure.description: Change the address or credentials Home Assistant uses to reach this Emby server. Your devices, entities and automations are kept.

data_description.host: The new IP address (e.g., 192.168.1.5) or hostname of your server.
data_description.api_key: Leave blank to keep the current API key.

reauth_confirm.title: Emby API key needed
reauth_confirm.description: {name} no longer accepts the API key Home Assistant is using. Create a new key in your Emby Dashboard under **Advanced > API Keys** and enter it below.

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to Emby Server. Check your IP and Port.
error.invalid_auth: Invalid API Key. Please verify the key in your Emby Dashboard.

abort.already_configured: This Emby server is already configured.
abort.reconfigure_successful: Connection details updated. The integration has been reloaded.
abort.reauth_successful: API key updated. The integration has been reloaded.
abort.wrong_server: That address belongs to a different Emby server. To switch servers, add it as a new integration instead.

init.title: Emby clients
init.description: Choose which Emby clients are devices in Home Assistant. Unticking a client removes its device and entities.

data_description.clients: Each ticked client becomes a device in Home Assistant, even when it's offline. Clients you don't tick are ignored. You can change this later under the settings cog.

init.title: New Emby client: {name}
init.description: {name} ({app}) connected to your Emby server but isn't in Home Assistant.

confirm.title: Add {name}?
confirm.description: Submit to add {name} as a device.

abort.ignored: {name} won't be added. You can still add it later under the integration's settings cog.

send_message.name: Send message
send_message.description: Shows a pop-up message on connected Emby clients.

timeout_ms.name: Timeout
timeout_ms.description: How long the message stays on screen.

config_entry_id.name: Emby server
config_entry_id.description: Only send to clients of this server. Leave empty for all servers.
